headline: 11.4% of bankers in a Dallas Fed survey say they restrict customers' AI agents
body: In a Dallas Fed survey of 70 bankers, for 11.4% of respondents, their institution or service provider had taken steps to restrict customers' AI agent activity on online banking platforms. Another 22.9% said they planned to introduce restrictions within six months.
note: The findings suggest banks are still developing policies for AI agents, and the survey covers one Federal Reserve district only.

figure.label: bankers whose institution took steps to restrict AI agents

evidence.text: In a recently released survey of 70 bankers, the Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas found that 11.4% said their institution or service provider had taken steps to restrict existing or prospective customers’ AI agent activity on online banking platforms.
Another 22.9% said they planned to introduce restrictions within the next six months.
More than a quarter of respondents, 27.1%, said they did not know whether their institution or service provider had restricted AI-agent activity.
Meanwhile, 38.6% said no restrictions had been implemented and were not planned.
The Dallas Fed collected responses between Oct. 27 and Nov. 4 from bankers in its Eleventh Federal Reserve District.
The survey noted that the results provide a regional snapshot of how financial institutions are approaching AI-agent access rather than a measure of policies across the U.S. banking industry.
